fan-out.why: A queue absorbs the spike and lets each channel scale and respect rate limits independently. A single sequential sender works but takes far too long; a synchronous request times out.

no-duplicates.why: Queues give at-least-once delivery; idempotency keys make the second attempt a no-op.

provider-outage.why: Backoff avoids hammering a struggling provider, failover keeps delivery going, and a dead-letter queue keeps poison messages from blocking the rest.

quiet-hours.why: Honour preferences by deferring rather than dropping; define which categories may override them.

spike-rate.why: 1,000,000 ÷ 60 ≈ 16,667 per second, which is why it has to be spread over workers and providers.
